homebrew.name: rooted-city
homebrew.title: The Rooted City
homebrew.credit: Original homebrew for The Rooted City, a D&D 5e campaign: woods, fey, bent beasts, the Heartwood and their cooking.
homebrew.desc: Woods and fey materials, bent beasts, craftable items, meals and cultivation for The Rooted City and any forest campaign.

materials.name: Vesperwood Alder Plank
materials.desc: Pale alder that blushes blood-red as it dries. It drinks water without rotting, which is why boatwrights pay double for it.

materials.name: Seasoned Alder Redwood
materials.desc: Alder heartwood left a full year under the eaves until it runs a deep oxblood red. It keeps the damp out and, the Verge-folk say, the oath in.

materials.name: Alder Catkin
materials.desc: Soft brown catkins that shed gold dust in early spring. Boiled they give a rust-red dye and a bitter tea.

materials.name: Alder Red Dye
materials.desc: A deep, slow red dye that does not run in water. Boatwrights use it on hulls, and bell-founders on the ropes.

recipe.lore: Catkins and fresh alder shavings boiled down with ash and fixed with vinegar.

materials.name: Heartwood Bark
materials.desc: Thick bark from the Heartwood's true trees, warm to the hand like a sleeping animal. It resists fire poorly but cuts almost not at all, and a cut seals itself over a night.

materials.name: Heartwood Resin
materials.desc: Amber, faintly green sap that wells from the Heartwood's trunks at dusk. It closes wounds as it closes bark, and a drop of it is worth a day's wage in any clinic.

materials.name: Heartwood Burl
materials.desc: A fist-sized knot of living wood cut from the base of a Heartwood trunk. It is heavy as iron and warm as bread, and it remembers its shape after a blow.

materials.name: Heartwood Core
materials.desc: The pith of a Heartwood tree: a dense, honey-coloured heart that pulses once an hour like a slow drum. Smiths of the Order believed it could knit a shattered limb. Taking it provokes the whole wood.

materials.name: Thornwood Limb
materials.desc: A straight, hard limb of blackthorn, studded with thorns that must be shaved down before use. Good for staves and for stinging hands.

materials.name: Briar Cane
materials.desc: Long, supple canes of blackberry briar. They weave into baskets, snares and thorn-fences.

materials.name: Hollow Reed
materials.desc: Straight river reed with a clean bore. Pipe-makers, dart-makers and thieves all want them.

materials.name: Moss Felt
materials.desc: A tight mat of forest moss pressed between boards and dried until it holds like felt. It muffles footsteps and keeps the damp out of boots.

materials.name: Beard-lichen Dye
materials.desc: A pale grey-green dye boiled from beard lichen. The colour of a Verge-folk cloak.

materials.name: Oak-gall Ink
materials.desc: Black ink made from oak galls and iron salts. It bites into paper and does not fade; the Archive buys it by the cask.

materials.name: Birch Bark Sheet
materials.desc: Thin, white and waterproof bark that peels in sheets. It takes a pen as well as paper does.

materials.name: Rowan Twig
materials.desc: A twig of rowan with a red berry-cluster still on it. Hung over a door it keeps small fey from walking in without asking.

materials.name: Heartyew Stave
materials.desc: A seasoned stave of old churchyard yew, half sap-wood and half heart-wood. It makes the best bows in the country, and no one will say why.

materials.name: Spear-ash Haft
materials.desc: Straight-grained ash, dried slowly in the rafters. It takes a blow and gives it back.

materials.name: Hazel Rod
materials.desc: A forked hazel rod cut at dawn from a tree that has never been pruned. Diviners and fishermen swear by it.

materials.name: Bentwood
materials.desc: Bark and branch grown through a beast and kept in its shape. It splinters easily and the splinters fester; it is still better cord-wood than anything else the Heartwood leaves.

materials.name: Bent Thorn
materials.desc: A long, backward-barbed thorn from a bent beast's hide. It lodges in a wound and keeps its grip.

materials.name: Rootbound Bone
materials.desc: Bone with roots grown into it, grey on the outside and green in the marrow. Carvers value it because it does not split.

materials.name: Bent Heart
materials.desc: A beast's heart wrapped in root, still faintly warm. Cooks and alchemists pay for it; the Keepers do not like to see it carried.

materials.name: Phase Silk
materials.desc: Strand-thin silk that flickers out of sight when held in the wrong light. It takes dye only from the Feywild's own flowers.

materials.name: Phase Fang
materials.desc: A hollow fang that shimmers between being there and not. A few drops of its venom still blink the unwary.

materials.name: Gilded Bark
materials.desc: A plate of bark from the Orchard's wyvern, flaking gold on one face and rotted green on the other. Armourers will pay for it; so will the House whose emblem it was.

materials.name: Blossom-rot Stinger
materials.desc: A wyvern's stinger grown through with blossoms. It holds a single, vicious dose.

materials.name: Rotblossom Sac
materials.desc: A bloated sac of spores. Burst it in a closed room, and regret it.

materials.name: Glamour Dew
materials.desc: Dew gathered from a faerie ring before the sun touches it. It makes things look a little more like what you wish they were.

materials.name: Faerie-ring Loam
materials.desc: Dark crumbling soil from inside a ring of mushrooms. Anything planted in it grows a little faster and a little stranger.

materials.name: Moonmilk
materials.desc: A pale, faintly sweet milk wrung from moonlit stone by the Court's herd-pixies. It brings sleep that no nightmare can pass.

materials.name: Gossamer Thread
materials.desc: Spun by lantern moths and heron-spiders, finer than hair and stronger than hemp. It does not take dye, and glints at dusk.

materials.name: Lantern-moth Wing
materials.desc: A powder-soft wing that glows a pale green in the dark. A dozen make a lamp that burns without oil for a night.

materials.name: Bramble-sprite Wing
materials.desc: A paper-thin, veined wing no longer than a thumbnail. It hums when it is near a stiff breeze.

materials.name: Dryad's Tear
materials.desc: A drop of amber sap a dryad weeps when her tree is cut. It remembers the grief and gives it, in small measure, to whoever holds it.

materials.name: Dryad Bloom
materials.desc: A blossom that opens only on a dryad's tree, in the hour she wishes it. It never wilts while the dryad lives.

materials.name: Oak-stag Antler
materials.desc: A branching antler that carries leaves each spring, even after it is cut. It makes handles that will not slip.

materials.name: Oak-stag Heart
materials.desc: A deep red, wood-grained heart that tastes of oak and wet earth.

materials.name: Oak-stag Venison
materials.desc: Dark, fine-grained meat that tastes of acorn and rain.

materials.name: Mosshound Pelt
materials.desc: A pelt matted with living moss. It is warm, hard to see in the wood and smells of rain.

materials.name: Mosshound Tooth
materials.desc: A short, green-stained fang.

materials.name: Court Thorn
materials.desc: A black thorn from the Court's briar-sworn. Its point is finer than any needle and dulls only after the wielder dies.

materials.name: Iron-wired Glove
materials.desc: A fine leather glove wrapped in iron wire, worn by the Briar-sworn so they can hold iron without burning. A fey who wears it cannot take it off.

materials.name: Market Heron Feather
materials.desc: A long grey feather from the herons that wade the Hollow Market's flooded stair. It writes by itself, if what it writes is true.

materials.name: Fey Pollen
materials.desc: A golden dust that rises from Court flower-beds in the evening. It makes you sneeze truth.

materials.name: Courtfire Ash
materials.desc: Grey ash from a Court bonfire. It does not smell of smoke but of cut grass.

materials.name: Satyr Pipe Reed
materials.desc: A pale reed cut at the exact hour the fey piper prefers. It carries a note across a wood.

materials.name: Oldest-root Sap
materials.desc: The sap of the oldest root under the city. It runs clear as water and cools the hand. The Court gives it only for a memory.

materials.name: Alder Seed Pouch
materials.desc: A pouch of alder seeds, small as dust. A gift Thalenne accepts: a grove that was cut, promised back.

materials.name: Thornseed
materials.desc: A hard, black seed that sprouts a thicket in a day wherever it is planted. Skerrin's people give it for a cherished memory, and never say what it will do.

materials.name: Lake Vesper Water
materials.desc: Clear lake water from the middle of Lake Vesper, drawn from a boat on a flat calm. It does not warm in the hand.

materials.name: Wild Garlic Ramson
materials.desc: Broad green leaves with a hot, garlicky bite. They carpet the wood floor in spring.

materials.name: Acorn Meal
materials.desc: Ground acorn, leached of its bitterness. A forager's flour.

materials.name: Sweet Chestnut
materials.desc: A glossy, tight-skinned nut that roasts in its shell.

materials.name: Hazelnut
materials.desc: A small, sweet, hard-shelled nut.

materials.name: Wood Sorrel
materials.desc: Clover-like leaves with a lemony tang.

materials.name: Bilberry
materials.desc: A dark blue berry that stains the tongue and the hands.

materials.name: Elderflower
materials.desc: Creamy flower heads with a sweet, musky scent.

materials.name: Birch Sap
materials.desc: Clear, thin sap tapped from birch in early spring. It is faintly sweet.

materials.name: Forest Maple Syrup
materials.desc: Thick amber syrup boiled down from maple sap.

materials.name: Pine Nut
materials.desc: A pale, soft, oily nut from a pine cone.

materials.name: Mistwood Morel
materials.desc: A honeycombed, nutty mushroom that fruits only where the mist lies.

materials.name: Gilded Chanterelle
materials.desc: A golden, apricot-scented mushroom that grows in the shade of old oaks.

materials.name: Moonapple
materials.desc: A small silver-skinned apple that ripens only under a full moon.

materials.name: Glamour Plum
materials.desc: A plum that tastes of whatever you were hoping for.

materials.name: Silverberry
materials.desc: A small, silver, round berry that rolls in the palm like a die.

materials.name: Dreamfig
materials.desc: A soft purple fig that makes you very sleepy and very contented.

materials.name: Wishnut
materials.desc: A hazelnut that grows only on trees by a Court well. It rattles with a small, bright sound.

materials.name: Faerie Honey
materials.desc: Honey from fey bees: thick, clear, and warm even in the cold. It makes any promise sound sweet.

materials.name: Court Flour
materials.desc: Flour from the Court's own wheat. Bread made of it feeds twice what you would expect.

materials.name: Heartwood Honey
materials.desc: Dark honey from bees that feed on Heartwood blossom. It tastes of resin and heals small hurts.

materials.name: Hollow Puffball
materials.desc: A white puffball that grows in Hollow Market cellars. Squeezed, it breathes a drowsy smoke.

materials.name: Sweetfern Frond
materials.desc: Anise-flavoured fern fronds, popular with goatherds and goat-stew.

materials.name: Cattail Shoot
materials.desc: The pale heart of a young cattail; it tastes of cucumber.

materials.name: Alder-bank Trout
materials.desc: A fat, speckled trout from the Vesper brook.

items.name: Heartwood Balm
items.effect: Amber-green balm that tastes of pine and honey. Drink or smear on a wound as an action: regain 3d4 + 3 hit points and end one poison or disease effect of 2nd level or lower. Wounds it closes leave a faint bark-like scar.

recipe.lore: Resin closes the wound, moss soothes it and wax keeps it from running off before it sets.

items.name: Mossbed Draught
items.effect: A cool, earthy draught. Drink as an action: regain 2d4 + 2 hit points and gain advantage on your next saving throw against poison within the hour.

recipe.lore: Chanterelle is a quiet healer, and honey carries it past the tongue and into the blood.

items.name: Glamour Philter
items.effect: A shimmering, oddly sweet liquid. For 1 hour after drinking it, you can change your appearance as the disguise self spell, once, without concentration.

recipe.lore: Dew caught on a morning web still holds the shapes it reflected; salt fixes one of them.

items.name: Moonmilk Nightcap
items.effect: Pale, warm and faintly silver. Drink it just before a long rest: you cannot be woken by dreams or nightmares during the rest, and you regain one extra Hit Die when it ends.

recipe.lore: The milk of the moon is a slow thing; figs make it sleepy and honey makes it stay.

items.name: Sprite's Leap
items.effect: A fizzing, sky-blue draught. For 1 minute your jump distance is tripled and you take no damage from falling.

recipe.lore: The wing's lift survives a long steeping if it is sweetened and then sharpened.

items.name: Dryad's Kiss Elixir
items.effect: A rose-scented elixir that clings to the lips. For 1 hour you have advantage on Charisma checks against fey and beasts, and you can cast speak with animals at will.

recipe.lore: A dryad's tear remembers every kindness done beneath her tree; honey and flowers give it a mouth to say so.

items.name: Elixir of Oldroot
items.effect: Thick, dark sap that smells of rain on old earth. Drink as an action: regain 8d4 + 8 hit points and end one curse or disease.

recipe.lore: The root that has outlived the city also outlives most things that ail its drinker.

items.name: Rowan Oil
items.effect: Red-gold oil pressed from rowan berries. Applied to a weapon or piece of ammunition (1 minute), it counts as magical and deals an extra 1d4 force damage against fey for 1 hour.

recipe.lore: Rowan is the old gate-keeper; oil carries its refusal into a blade.

items.name: Quietwood Pitch
items.effect: Black, sticky pitch that never quite sets. Rubbed onto boots or hooves (1 minute), it deadens sound for 1 hour: advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to move silently.

recipe.lore: Felt swallows footsteps, and pitch makes the felt cling to the sole.

items.name: Heartwood Rosin
items.effect: Sticky green-gold resin. Applied to a weapon (1 minute), the next hit within 1 hour that deals damage to a creature entangles it in grasping tendrils (Strength save, DC 13, or restrained until the end of its next turn).

recipe.lore: Resin glues, thorn bites, and the Heartwood is happy to help it hold.

items.name: Gilded Wyvern Venom
items.effect: Golden, metallic-smelling venom. Injury: apply to a weapon (1 action). A creature hit must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save or take 7d6 poison damage (half on a save). Keeps 1 week once applied.

recipe.lore: The bloom keeps the sting alive; vinegar sets it, wax stops it spoiling.

items.name: Rotblossom Spores
items.effect: A pouch of grey-pink spores. Inhaled: a creature in a 5-foot cube must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution save or be poisoned for 1 hour; while poisoned it also takes 1d4 poison damage at the start of each turn for 1 minute.

recipe.lore: The sac is dried and ground; ash keeps it a dust.

items.name: Phase-fang Venom
items.effect: Pale, faintly flickering venom. Injury: a creature hit must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution save or be unable to take reactions and have its speed halved for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns.

recipe.lore: A phase spider's bite is half in this world; the venom keeps its half out of step.

items.name: Dreamdust
items.effect: Soft, white powder with a smell of baked pears. Inhaled: a creature in a 5-foot cube must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution save or fall asleep for 1 minute (until it takes damage or is shaken awake).

recipe.lore: Puffball spores dull the waking mind, and the fig makes the dull things pleasant.

items.name: Briar-sting Draught
items.effect: Greenish, bitter draught. Injury: a creature hit must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution save or take 2d6 poison damage and be poisoned until the end of its next turn.

recipe.lore: The thorns of the bent are crushed, steeped and strained. They are still the Heartwood's, and the wound remembers.

items.name: Sapheart Arrows (10)
items.effect: Ten arrows with amber sap on the heads. A creature hit is sticky with sap: its speed is reduced by 10 feet until it spends an action scraping it off.

recipe.lore: Bentwood sap sets in the wound and makes a bad thing worse.

items.name: Court-ash Arrows (10)
items.effect: Ten arrows fletched in grey and tipped with a pinch of Court ash. A creature hit is outlined in faint flame until the end of your next turn: attacks against it have advantage and it cannot benefit from being invisible.

recipe.lore: Faerie fire without the spell: the ash holds the light until it is struck.

items.name: Hollowreed Darts (20)
items.effect: Twenty slim reed darts for a blowgun. 1 piercing damage. A pinch of poison fits the hollow shaft.

recipe.lore: Cut the reed on the knot, whittle one end, tuft the other.

items.name: Scroll of Green Tangle
items.effect: Spell scroll of entangle (DC 13). Cast from the scroll as normal.

recipe.lore: The sheet takes the ink; the bentwood gives it a reason to grow.

items.name: Scroll of Barkskin
items.effect: Spell scroll of barkskin (DC 13). Cast from the scroll as normal.

recipe.lore: Bark on bark: the Heartwood does not mind being copied.

items.name: Scroll of Misty Step
items.effect: Spell scroll of misty step. Cast from the scroll as normal.

recipe.lore: Silk from a creature that steps sideways; the ink finishes the step.

items.name: Scroll of Plant Growth
items.effect: Spell scroll of plant growth. Cast from the scroll as normal.

recipe.lore: Sap in the ink makes a spell that wants to be read aloud.

items.name: Scroll of Animal Friendship
items.effect: Spell scroll of animal friendship (DC 13). Cast from the scroll as normal.

recipe.lore: Fey hounds know the tongue of beasts and are happy to lend it.

items.name: Heartyew Longbow
items.effect: A +1 longbow. Arrows loosed from it make no more sound than a breath, and you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to stay hidden after you fire.

recipe.lore: The yew grows over graves; it keeps its own counsel, and so does the bow.

items.name: Thornwood Quarterstaff
items.effect: A +1 quarterstaff. Once per dawn, as a bonus action, you can sprout thorns along it for 1 minute: hits deal an extra 1d6 piercing damage.

recipe.lore: Court thorns do not lose their will to grow, only their roots.

items.name: Antler Knife
items.effect: A +1 dagger with a stag-antler hilt. On a critical hit, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

recipe.lore: Antler remembers the charge it was made for.

items.name: Warden's Sickle
items.effect: A sickle with a rowan haft. It counts as magical against fey and deals an extra 1d4 force damage to them. Harvesting with it never spoils the plant.

recipe.lore: Rowan and iron are the two things the fey ask politely about.

items.name: Spear-ash Spear
items.effect: A well-balanced spear. It counts as magical for overcoming resistance, and when thrown, it returns to your hand at the end of your turn if you drop it within 30 feet.

recipe.lore: Ash flies true and returns to those who cut it fairly.

items.name: Hazel Diviner's Rod
items.effect: A forked hazel rod. Held in both hands, it dips toward fresh water within 100 feet. Once per dawn you can ask it where the nearest safe path out of the wood lies, as the find the path spell's direction (no duration).

recipe.lore: Hazel remembers where the water goes.

items.name: Mossweave Leather
items.effect: Leather armor lined with moss felt. While you wear it, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks in forests and swamps. It is damp and smells like a forest floor.

recipe.lore: The felt does the hiding; the leather only holds it up.

items.name: Redwood Shield
items.effect: A +1 shield of seasoned alder redwood. It is as heavy as it looks, and it shrugs off water, fire and the Heartwood's roots: advantage on saves against being grappled or restrained by plants.

recipe.lore: Oxblood wood that will not rot, and a rim of leather to keep the edge honest.

items.name: Heartwood Bark Mail
items.effect: +1 medium armor (attunement). While you are in a forest or standing on living earth and are not at 0 hit points, you regain 2 hit points at the start of each of your turns. Bark knits over its wounds each night.

recipe.lore: It has to be worn like a living thing: gently, and with permission.

items.name: Gilded Barkbuckler
items.effect: +1 shield (attunement). Once per long rest, when you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to gain +3 AC against it. The gilded bark hums when radiant power is near.

recipe.lore: The Brightwater wyvern's plate is nearly impossible to dent, and the shield remembers it.

items.name: Stag-hide Vest
items.effect: Light armor. Your walking speed increases by 5 feet while you wear it, and you do not suffer disadvantage from difficult terrain made of non-magical plants.

recipe.lore: A stag clears a thicket without noticing it.

items.name: Lantern-moth Jar
items.effect: A glass jar with a living moth wing in a drop of dew. It sheds dim light in a 20-foot radius. As an action you can have it shed bright light in a 15-foot radius instead, for 10 minutes once per day.

recipe.lore: The wing keeps the shimmer of the moth's own lantern, and the dew keeps it wet.

items.name: Mossfelt Boots
items.effect: Your footsteps are silent on soil, moss and leaves. You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to move silently while wearing them.

recipe.lore: Felt-soled boots, from the ground up.

items.name: Verge Cloak
items.effect: Attunement. While you are in a forest and have not moved on your turn, creatures more than 30 feet away have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to see you, and you can hide in lightly obscured areas.

recipe.lore: Dye the cloak the colour of the Verge and let the dew do the rest.

items.name: Phase-silk Cloak
items.effect: Attunement. Once per dawn, you can cast misty step from the cloak as a bonus action. A pale thread of the silk is always slightly out of step with the rest of it.

recipe.lore: The silk that stepped aside from the world is stitched along the hem.

items.name: Gossamer Gloves
items.effect: While wearing the gloves, you have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed and can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down along ceilings, as long as your hands are free.

recipe.lore: Spider-silk for hands that want to be spiders.

items.name: Sprite-wing Cape
items.effect: Attunement. Once per long rest, as a bonus action, you gain a flying speed of 30 feet for 10 minutes. If you are still flying when it ends, you fall gently as if under feather fall.

recipe.lore: Four sprite wings, sewn onto a cloak by someone patient, and the bloom to keep them alive.

items.name: Ring of Rowan Warding
items.effect: Attunement. You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and fey cannot charm you without your consent. It tingles whenever a fey creature is within 30 feet.

recipe.lore: A ring cut from a single twist of redwood, with the old rowan charm carved inside.

items.name: Ring of the Mossfast
items.effect: Attunement. Difficult terrain made of non-magical plants costs you no extra movement, and you have advantage on saving throws against being grappled or restrained by plants.

recipe.lore: A bent heart keeps the shape of the root it grew through.

items.name: Wand of Brambles
items.effect: Attunement. 7 charges, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn (on a 1, it turns to a bramble). Expend 1 charge to cast entangle (DC 13), or 2 charges to cast spike growth (DC 13).

recipe.lore: A wand that wants to be a briar.

items.name: Staff of the Green Court
items.effect: Attunement by a druid, ranger or cleric. 10 charges, regaining 1d6 + 4 at dawn. Expend charges to cast: pass without trace (1), entangle (1), barkskin (2), plant growth (3), cure wounds as a 3rd-level spell (3). The staff itself is a +1 quarterstaff while you are attuned.

recipe.lore: A staff cut from a tree that said yes.

items.name: Satyr's Pipes
items.effect: A set of reed pipes. You have advantage on Charisma (Performance) checks made with them. Once per dawn, you can play a tune that calms animals: as the animal friendship spell (DC 12).

recipe.lore: The reeds that grow in a satyr's meadow like to be played.

items.name: Court-flame Pipe
items.effect: A short pipe of blackthorn. Played as an action, it casts dancing lights (no concentration, 1 minute, lasts as long as you keep playing). Once per dawn it can cast faerie fire (DC 13) from its notes.

recipe.lore: The Court plays its light as well as dances it.

items.name: Moss Horn
items.effect: A hunting horn wrapped in moss felt. It can be heard up to 3 miles away, and only by those you want to hear it.

recipe.lore: A horn that gives its call to those who want to hear it.

items.name: Wishnut Charm
items.effect: Attunement. Once per long rest, when you fail an ability check, you can roll a d4 and add it to the check, possibly turning the failure into a success.

recipe.lore: A wishnut held on a thread. Luck, like acorns, likes to fall close to where it began.

items.name: Silverberry Brooch
items.effect: Attunement. Once per dawn, when you roll a 1 on an attack roll, ability check or saving throw, you can reroll and must use the new result.

recipe.lore: A silverberry dried hard and set in silver.

items.name: Heartsong Locket
items.effect: Attunement. Once per long rest, you can cast charm person, calm emotions or speak with plants, as a 3rd-level spell (DC 15). The locket holds a petal that never wilts.

recipe.lore: A petal of a dryad's own bloom, kept in a frame of wax and silver.

items.name: Heron-feather Cloak
items.effect: Attunement. You have advantage on Charisma (Deception) and Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks, and once per long rest you can cast the nondetection spell on yourself (no components).

recipe.lore: A herons' wardrobe: the Market's birds know what everyone in it keeps hidden.

items.name: Stagheart Pendant
items.effect: Attunement. Your Strength score becomes 18 while you wear it if it is lower, and you have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to charge or leap.

recipe.lore: A stag's heart, dried and carved, still beats at a faint pace in sleep.

items.name: Tangle-vine Snare
items.effect: A coil of living briar and cord. Set as an action (DC 12 Survival): the first creature to enter the square must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity save or be restrained until it escapes (DC 12 Strength).

recipe.lore: A trap that grows back.

items.name: Briar Basket
items.effect: A woven basket that holds 40 pounds without strain. A wet basket stays dry inside.

recipe.lore: Wind it round, tie it off and hang it on a hook.

items.name: Moss Bedroll
items.effect: A bedroll stuffed with dried moss. You have advantage on saving throws against cold when you sleep in it.

recipe.lore: Felt-stuffed canvas: dry and warm.

items.name: Birchbark Scroll Case
items.effect: A waterproof tube for scrolls and maps. It floats.

recipe.lore: Rolled, waxed, capped.

items.name: Woodwarden's Harvesting Kit
items.effect: A harvesting kit with rowan-handled knives. Add 1d4 to harvesting checks on plants and fey.

recipe.lore: Tools for taking only what the woods give.

items.name: Heartwood Pruning Shears
items.effect: Pruning shears of old iron and bark. When used to harvest from the Heartwood, you cause no outrage on a roll of 10 or more.

recipe.lore: A tool the wood has agreed to.

items.name: Ramson Pemmican
items.effect: A day's ration of dried meat, tallow and wild garlic. It keeps for a month.

recipe.lore: Pound, pack, wait.

items.name: Acorn Hardtack
items.effect: A day's ration of dense acorn-meal biscuit. It keeps for a month and tastes of very little.

recipe.lore: Mill, mix, bake hard.

items.name: Tin Lantern
items.effect: In ordinary hands it gives no light. It glows green and warms within 30 feet of a village lamp, the Hollow Market's stair or a fey creature. The bearer has advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to find the way back to the last place they slept.

items.name: Aldous's Sash
items.effect: A Keeper's sash. Keepers recognise it as a sign you can be trusted: advantage on Charisma checks to persuade a Keeper.

items.name: Thorne Seal
items.effect: Opens the Water Gates and any Thorne lock, and gives passage on a Thorne barge.

items.name: Thawwater
items.effect: Clear, cold water that never quite thaws. Drinking a draught heals as a potion of greater healing and ends one level of exhaustion. 3 draughts.

items.name: Heartwood Acorn
items.effect: When thrown, it casts entangle (DC 14) at the point it lands. Consumable.

items.name: Pouch of Alder Seeds
items.effect: A gift Thalenne accepts, carried in a leather pouch. Consumable.

items.name: Lamp of the Quiet
items.effect: Lit as an action, it gives each creature within 20 feet advantage on saving throws against being frightened, for up to 1 hour each day.

items.name: Keepers' Mason's Tools
items.effect: Count as mason's tools. Advantage on checks to cut, shape or raise stone and iron-bound bands.

items.name: Heartsap
items.effect: One vial. Saves one servant or pseudodragon that drank little of the Tithe and has not yet turned. Nobody who has drunk deeply can be saved.

items.name: Thornseed
items.effect: Planted in a street, it brings the Heartwood there within a day. Consumable.

items.name: Lake Water Flask
items.effect: Poured into a failing spring, it keeps the water clear for a month. Consumable.

items.name: Mill-bell
items.effect: About 90 pounds. When rung within 300 feet, bent beasts stop (as Bell-struck).

items.name: Chapel Bell
items.effect: About 150 pounds. When rung within 300 feet, bent beasts stop (as Bell-struck).

items.name: Landing Bell
items.effect: About 60 pounds. When rung within 300 feet, bent beasts stop (as Bell-struck).

items.name: Weir Rings
items.effect: Attunement. You have a swimming speed equal to your walking speed. Once per long rest you can cast water walk.

items.name: Gilded Pruners
items.effect: A +1 dagger. Advantage on Wisdom (Nature) checks and attack rolls against plant creatures. Cutting the Heartwood with it does not provoke it.

items.name: Sickle of Plenty
items.effect: A +1 sickle. Once per long rest you can use it to harvest enough from a field or a hedge to feed ten people for a day (as create food and water).

items.name: Ledger-pen
items.effect: Advantage on Investigation checks to find an error or a lie in written accounts. Once per long rest, cast identify.

items.name: Name-tags
items.effect: Attunement. A string of small tags. Once per long rest you can speak a dead creature's name and cast speak with dead without components.

items.name: Ramson Broth
items.effect: A thin green broth sharp with wild garlic. For 8 hours you have advantage on saving throws against the poisoned condition from spoiled food or water.

recipe.lore: Boil the greens and let them give up their sharpness.

items.name: Acorn Porridge
items.effect: Thick, leached acorn meal cooked with water. It sticks to the ribs. You gain 1d4 temporary hit points that last 8 hours.

recipe.lore: Soak out the bitterness, then boil until it holds a spoon.

items.name: Roast Chestnuts
items.effect: Warm, split and smoking from the fire. You feel comforted: for 8 hours you have advantage on saving throws against exhaustion from cold.

recipe.lore: A cut across the shell, a hot pan and a lot of patience.

items.name: Bilberry Compote
items.effect: Dark and tart. For 8 hours you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight in dim light.

recipe.lore: Stew the berries with a little honey.

items.name: Planked Trout
items.effect: River trout baked on a cedar plank over embers. A good meal: you gain 1d4 temporary hit points that last 8 hours.

recipe.lore: Split, salt and lay on a plank by the fire.

items.name: Cattail Fritters
items.effect: Fried cattail shoots in a crisp coat of acorn meal. You gain 1d4 temporary hit points that last 8 hours.

recipe.lore: Peel the shoots, dip them and fry them quick.

items.name: Pine-nut Loaf
items.effect: A dense, oily loaf that keeps for days on the road. You do not suffer exhaustion from a missed meal on the day you eat it.

recipe.lore: Grind the nuts into the dough; bake until it knocks hollow.

items.name: Elderflower Cordial
items.effect: Sweet, floral and cooling. For 8 hours you have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned by heat or thirst, and you smell faintly of summer.

recipe.lore: Steep the flowers in sugar water until they give it up.

items.name: Misty Morel Stew
items.effect: A rich, smoky stew. You gain 1d6 + 2 temporary hit points that last 8 hours.

recipe.lore: Venison and morels stewed down until the broth is dark.

items.name: Gilded Chanterelle Roast
items.effect: Golden mushrooms roasted whole in their own juices. When you spend a Hit Die to heal during a short rest within 8 hours, you regain an extra 2 hit points.

recipe.lore: Slow heat and a very little salt.

items.name: Venison in Moonapple
items.effect: Venison braised with moonapple until it is almost sweet. For 8 hours you have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to jump or climb.

recipe.lore: The apple takes the gamey edge off the meat.

items.name: Glamour Plum Tart
items.effect: A purple-glazed pastry that tastes different to each person. For 8 hours you have advantage on Charisma (Deception) and (Performance) checks, but also disadvantage on Insight checks: you are a little too pleased with yourself.

recipe.lore: Plums folded into pastry; no one can say how it ends.

items.name: Hazelnut Honey Cake
items.effect: A dense, nutty cake. For 8 hours you have advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) checks.

recipe.lore: Ground nuts, flour and honey, baked slow.

items.name: Maple-glazed Trout
items.effect: Trout lacquered with maple. For 8 hours your hit point maximum is increased by 5 and you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened by hunger or exhaustion.

recipe.lore: Glaze, rest, glaze again.

items.name: Sorrel and Ramson Soup
items.effect: A sharp green soup. For 8 hours you have resistance to poison damage.

recipe.lore: Wild garlic and sorrel are older than most medicines.

items.name: Birch Sap Flapjack
items.effect: A chewy, golden oat bar. For 8 hours your walking speed is increased by 5 feet.

recipe.lore: Sap boiled to syrup, folded into oats.

items.name: Courtbread
items.effect: A sweet, close-crumbed loaf, as sold in the Hollow Market. For 8 hours you have advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks against fey.

recipe.lore: Bread baked as the Court bakes it: slowly and without regrets.

items.name: Wild Berry Pie
items.effect: A deep-filled pie. You gain 1d6 + 2 temporary hit points that last 8 hours.

recipe.lore: Berries under a lid, left to sing in the oven.

items.name: Sweetfern Tea
items.effect: A sweet, anise-tinged tea. When you finish a short rest within 8 hours of drinking it, you regain 1d4 hit points.

recipe.lore: Steep the fronds and strain.

items.name: Rootwarm Hotpot
items.effect: A pot of tubers and venison kept simmering. For 8 hours you have resistance to cold damage.

recipe.lore: Everything in the pot, and the pot on the coals.

items.name: Dreamfig Pudding
items.effect: A heavy, dark pudding. When you finish a long rest within 8 hours of eating it, you regain one extra Hit Die and your exhaustion level is reduced by 1 (in addition to the usual).

recipe.lore: Figs steamed in their own sugar until they relax.

items.name: Silverberry Preserve
items.effect: A glittering preserve. Once within 8 hours, when you roll a 1 on an attack roll, ability check or saving throw, you can reroll it.

recipe.lore: Berries set in syrup; they keep their luck as long as they stay silvered.

items.name: Wishnut Brittle
items.effect: A hard, caramel-brown brittle. Once within 8 hours, when you fail an ability check, you can roll a d4 and add it to the result.

recipe.lore: Nuts cooked in sugar until they crackle.

items.name: Faerie Honey Cake
items.effect: A soft, glistening cake. For 8 hours you have advantage on Charisma checks against fey, and you cannot be charmed by them without your consent.

recipe.lore: Honey that kept its promises, folded into a cake.

items.name: Stagheart Stew
items.effect: A dark, almost-purple stew. For 8 hours you have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and your carrying capacity is doubled.

recipe.lore: Heart and haunch, slow-cooked for most of a night.

items.name: Heartwood-glazed Venison
items.effect: Venison glazed with heartwood honey. You gain 2d6 + 3 temporary hit points that last 8 hours.

recipe.lore: Glaze at the last moment; it burns easily.

items.name: Puffball Risotto
items.effect: A pale, creamy dish. For 8 hours you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened, and you cannot be put to sleep by magic.

recipe.lore: Slice the puffball while it is still white inside.

items.name: Moonmilk Porridge
items.effect: A pale, shimmering porridge. When you finish a long rest within 8 hours of eating it, you regain one extra Hit Die.

recipe.lore: Moonmilk thickens as it cools, and so does the person who eats it.

items.name: Gilded Chanterelle Pie
items.effect: A golden pastry. When you spend Hit Dice to heal during a short rest within 8 hours, you regain an extra 1d4 hit points per Hit Die.

recipe.lore: Chanterelles under a lid of pastry.

items.name: Evergreen Feast
items.effect: A feast that smells of rain, bread and a forest at morning. For 8 hours you gain 2d10 temporary hit points, advantage on saving throws against poison and fear, and immunity to the poisoned condition. It can only be eaten when everyone at the table is at peace.

recipe.lore: A feast cooked for eight: the Heartwood's gift, shared.

items.name: Banquet of the Green Court
items.effect: A table-length banquet of fruit, honey and roasted game. For 8 hours you have advantage on Charisma checks and saving throws against being charmed or frightened, and you can cast charm person once (DC 15) without a spell slot.

recipe.lore: A banquet laid out as the Court lays it: with more courses than anyone could count.

monsters.name: Bent Wolf
monsters.blurb: A wolf the forest has grown through: branches for ribs and a muzzle of bark. It hunts in packs of four to six and goes for whoever is already bleeding.

harvest.note: Cut the branches out before they splinter.

monsters.name: Bent Boar
monsters.blurb: A boar with roots for tusks and a coat of moss and burrs. It charges blindly, and what it hits stays hit.

harvest.note: A tusk grown with bark in it.

monsters.name: Bent Direwolf
monsters.blurb: A direwolf grown into the Heartwood, its flanks barked and its eyes pits of green. It leads the pack and does not stop for fire.

harvest.note: Take it while it is still warm.

monsters.name: Bent Owlbear
monsters.blurb: An owlbear with a crown of antler-like branches and moss in the hollows of its beak. It is slow to fall and very hard to turn.

monsters.name: Bent Phase Spider
monsters.blurb: A phase spider with thorns on its legs, stepping in and out of the world among the trunks. The Heartwood has not taught it to stop.

harvest.note: A hank, if it is cut before the thread steps away.

monsters.name: The Gilded Wyvern
monsters.blurb: Brightwater's gilded wyvern, half-grown into the Heartwood: golden scales gone to bark and a barbed tail blooming with thorn. It is a guardian by habit and a hunter by now.

harvest.note: The bloom is the stinger, grown through.

monsters.name: Briar-sworn
monsters.blurb: One of the Dawnbriar Court's sworn: a thin, thorn-armed figure in iron-wrapped gloves, silent and exact. It will not parley before the first blow.

harvest.note: Cut off the thorn cluster at the wrist.

monsters.name: Oakheart Stag
monsters.blurb: A stag with antlers like young oak limbs and a heart that glows faintly green when it runs. It is wary of people and fierce to anyone who corners it.

harvest.note: Cut at the burr, not the beam.

monsters.name: Mosshound
monsters.blurb: A grey, shaggy hound with a coat of living moss and eyes like lanterns. It follows fey and sometimes people it likes.

monsters.name: Lantern-moth Swarm
monsters.blurb: A cloud of soft, pale moths, each wing a small green lantern. They gather around the dying and sleepers and mean no harm unless the light is taken.

harvest.note: A swept handful of loose wings.

monsters.name: Bramble Sprite
monsters.blurb: A palm-sized thing of thorn and petal, always in motion. Mischievous and cheap to bribe with honey.

harvest.note: Only if it lets you. Sprites will bargain for them.

monsters.name: Court Dryad
monsters.blurb: A dryad of the Dawnbriar Court: pale-barked, quick to anger and bound to a single tree. She weeps resin on those she trusts.

harvest.note: Given, not taken. Nothing comes from an angry dryad.

monsters.name: Market Heron
monsters.blurb: A tall grey heron that stalks the Hollow Market's stair and is known to buy and sell secrets. It does not fight if it can bargain.

harvest.note: A feather, plucked while it listens.

monsters.name: Wishnut Squirrel
monsters.blurb: A grey squirrel the fey have been feeding. It buries wishnuts, forgets them and is certain they were lucky.

harvest.note: The squirrel hides them by habit. A good Survival check finds the cache.

monsters.name: Awakened Briar
monsters.blurb: A thicket that has been given a will and not told what for. It grabs and holds and does not hate.

monsters.name: Satyr Piper
monsters.blurb: A goat-legged piper who plays at the edge of the glade and watches who dances. He is neither friendly nor hostile until asked a favour.

harvest.note: He carves his own pipes; you can find the offcuts.

monsters.name: Heartwood Warden
monsters.blurb: A living trunk walking on its roots, bark as thick as a door and eyes like knotholes. It guards the Heartwood's oldest groves and does not mind who cuts, as long as it is told first.

harvest.note: From a warden that has been felled, or one that gives it freely.
Only from a felled warden, and the grove will remember.

gather.cond: Alder groves in spring, where the catkins shed their gold.
Any forest edge where the blackberry has taken a hedge.
Silver birch, peeled from the fallen trunks only.
Damp hollows under beech and oak in spring.
Shaded ground under old oak.
Sunny clearings in late summer.
Under old chestnut trees in autumn.
Hazel hedges in autumn, before the squirrels.
Stone-pine stands on dry ground.
Early spring, tapped from a living birch.
Boiled down from a sugar maple's sap in early spring.
Under old oak in autumn; it must be leached.
Blackthorn thickets and hedgerows.
gather.riskWhy: Thorns and the things that live in them.

gather.cond: A lone rowan near a path, cut with permission.
An unpruned hazel at dawn.
Fallen cones under alders by water.
A fey orchard, under a full moon.
A plum tree in a fairy ring, ripe at dusk.
Damp, mossy ground on misty mornings.
Gold-spotted mushrooms under old beech.
Wild court-wheat growing in an abandoned Dawnbriar clearing.
gather.riskWhy: The Court still watches its own clearings.

gather.cond: Open woodland on sandy soil.
Reedy glades where a satyr plays.
From spider webs at first light in a fey glade.
The dark loam inside a fairy ring.
The cold ash of a Court fire-circle.
Scattered around a glade where the moths have gathered.
From a stag, hunted fair.
Bark cut from the Heartwood's true trees.
Resin from the Heartwood's trunks at dusk.
Wild bees nesting in a Heartwood hollow.
Old churchyard yew, seasoned and cut where it falls.
A fey bramble in a moonlit hollow.
A lone fig in a fey clearing.
Squirrel caches, found by following the squirrel.
Damp, shaded glades after rain.
Golden dust from wyrmwood in bloom.
Dripping from limestone at night in a moonlit hollow.
Wild bees in a fey hollow.
Court thorn growing wild at the edge of a clearing.
A dryad's tree in spring, offered not taken.
Resin from a dryad's tree, given as a kindness.
Sap from the oldest root of the Heartwood.
A burl at the base of an old Heartwood trunk.
The heart of a felled warden, if the grove allows it.
gather.riskWhy: The wood remembers who cuts it.

gather.cond: Reed beds along the lake shore.
Reedy shallows.
Fished from a cold, clear stream.
Alders at the water's edge in early spring.
Bog fringes in summer.
Reedy glades where a satyr plays.
Fallen cones in the shallows.
Marsh webs at dawn.
Where the moths gather over still water.
Damp reed-bed hollows after rain.
Dripping from a limestone overhang above the water.
Water drawn from Lake Vesper at the old landing, after a prayer.
Wild garlic where the Heartwood has broken the paving.
Brambles pulled from a greened street.
Fallen cones under a street alder.
A rowan growing out of a courtyard.
Dropped in the street after a skirmish.
gather.riskWhy: The Court wants its gloves back.

gather.cond: From a young Heartwood trunk that has burst through the paving.
gather.riskWhy: The Heartwood wakes when it is cut.

gather.cond: Bark from a Heartwood root running under a street.
gather.riskWhy: The Heartwood wakes when it is cut.

gather.cond: Growing in the cracks of old stone.
Elder growing from a broken wall in summer.
The dark loam inside a fairy ring among old stones.
The cold ash of a Court fire-circle.
A plum tree that has taken over a courtyard.
Wild bees nesting in the ruins.
Court thorn growing wild among the stones.
A seed the Heartwood left in the stones, if the warden permits.

cultivation.needs: Shade and damp soil. Plant the bulbs in autumn and lift them in spring.
Shaded ground under a trellis; it self-seeds in a corner.
Acid soil and a little shade. Net the bushes against birds.
Grow it against a wall; pick the heads at midsummer.
Sandy, well-drained soil in half shade.
A sunken bed that stays wet all year.
A wet bed or a barrel of mud; cut after the first frost.
Anywhere. Keep it from becoming a hedge, which it will.
Wet soil and quiet; it is said to grow better when played to.
A young tree in good loam. It bears from the second year.
A hedge-row of hazel, coppiced in winter.
A dry slope and a stone pine; the cones take a long time.
Open sun and loose soil. It grows best in a circle; no one has said why.
A tapped birch, in early spring only.
A tree in a pot with a window to the moon; it fruits only at full moon.
A trained plum on a south wall, with a ring of stones around it.
A bramble that wants frost and moonlight; a cold frame works.
A fig in a warm corner. Do not sleep under it.
Plant the nut where no one will look. It fruits better when you forget it.
Wyrmwood in bloom, shaken over a sheet. Bees will come.
A damp, cool cellar and a bed of wood-ash and leaf mould.
Beech leaf-mould and a mossy log; keep it damp and dark.
A cool bed of sawdust; harvest before it opens, or it will sleep you.
A wet margin and a stand of alders; the trees choose their own rhythm.
A rowan planted at a gate, cut with permission.
A hazel in an old, unpruned grove; cut at dawn.
A blackthorn hedge; coppice it hard.
Alders in spring. They like their feet wet.
